subject: Money
title: The Pop and Aftermath
description: A short lesson to help you apply The Pop and Aftermath.

hook.text: The NASDAQ lost 78% between 2000 and 2002. It took 15 years to recover. Some stocks never came back.

buildup.text: Bubbles pop when a trigger—bad news, a rate hike, a fraud exposed—shakes confidence. Selling begets selling.

discovery.text: The crash phase is faster than the bubble. It took years to build and weeks to collapse.

twist.text: The real damage isn't paper losses. It's bankruptcies, job losses, and a decade of reduced investment and trust.

climax.text: After every bubble, regulations tighten. After every recovery, they loosen. The cycle resets.

quiz.question: How long did it take the NASDAQ to recover from the 2000 crash?
